text: A newborn can already pick out its mother’s voice from another woman’s, and will change the way it sucks to hear hers more often.
In a New York lab study, toddlers aged 12 to 19 months averaged 2,368 steps and 17 falls in every hour of free play.
By 30 months, most toddlers say about 50 words and put two or more together with an action word, like “doggie run”.
Most three-year-olds can keep a conversation going for two back-and-forth turns, and have started asking “who”, “what”, “where” or “why” questions.
Around four, children typically pass the classic false-belief test, predicting that someone will look for a toy where they last saw it, not where it now is.

source.label: Baillargeon, Scott & He, Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 2010

text: The grey matter of the brain’s cortex reaches its greatest volume at about 5.9 years of age, according to charts built from 123,984 MRI scans.
In November 1960, six-year-old Ruby Bridges walked into William Frantz Elementary in New Orleans, escorted by U.S. Marshals, to desegregate the school.

source.label: National Women's History Museum, Ruby Bridges biography

text: In a US study of 100 children, 65% had had an imaginary companion at some point by the age of seven.
In a US study, children of five to seven recalled 60% or more of events discussed at age three, while eight- and nine-year-olds recalled under 40%.
In October 1828, nine-year-old Clara Wieck, later Clara Schumann, first played for the public, at Leipzig’s Gewandhaus concert hall.
The World Health Organization counts adolescence from 10 to 19. There are more adolescents alive than ever before: 1.3 billion, one in six people on Earth.
Writing under the name Gul Makai, Malala Yousafzai was 11 when she began an anonymous diary for BBC Urdu about her wish to go to school.
From about 6 to 12, the outer layers of the brain’s hearing cortex mature, as children grow sharper at telling the sounds of language apart.

source.label: Moore & Linthicum, International Journal of Audiology, 2007

text: In August 1963 ‘Fingertips – Pt 2’ made Stevie Wonder the youngest solo artist ever to reach No. 1 on the US Billboard Hot 100.
In a study of 463 Danish choirboys, the median age at which the voice broke was 14.0 years.

source.label: Juul et al., International Journal of Andrology, 2007

text: In March 1955, 15-year-old Claudette Colvin refused to give up her seat on a segregated bus in Montgomery, nine months before Rosa Parks.
In 2007 Austria became the first EU country to lower the voting age to 16 in national elections, from 18.
Asked about personally meaningful songs, 1,891 people from many countries most often named ones released when they were about 17.
In April 2022 Japan lowered its age of adulthood from 20 to 18, the first change in roughly 140 years.
The mind’s raw speed at processing information peaks around 18 or 19; other abilities keep ripening for decades.
Sleep times drift later through the teens and reach their latest at around 20, a turning point proposed as a marker for the end of adolescence.

source.label: Nature News & Views on Roenneberg et al. (Current Biology), 2005

text: Until the Family Law Reform Act 1969, people in England and Wales came of full legal age at 21; the Act lowered it to 18.

source.label: legislation.gov.uk, Family Law Reform Act 1969, s.1

text: In January 2021, Amanda Gorman read ‘The Hill We Climb’ at a US presidential inauguration, the youngest inaugural poet in the country’s history.
In June 1925 Werner Heisenberg went to the island of Helgoland to ease his hay fever, and there set out the first mathematical framework of quantum mechanics.
On 28 November 1967, PhD student Jocelyn Bell, 24, recorded radio pulses one and a third seconds apart: the discovery of pulsars.

source.label: University of Cambridge, Journeys of discovery

text: The US Constitution sets 25 as the youngest age at which a person may serve in the House of Representatives.

source.label: US Constitution, Article I, Section 2 (National Archives transcript)

text: Across the European Union, young people leave their parents’ home at 26.2 on average (2024), from 21.4 in Finland to 31.3 in Croatia.
In the United States in 2024, the average age of a mother at the birth of her first child was 27.6.

source.label: CDC/NCHS FastStats: Births (Births: Final Data for 2024)

text: The brain’s white matter, the wiring that links its regions, reaches its greatest volume at about 28.7 years of age.

source.label: Bethlehem et al., Brain charts for the human lifespan, Nature, 2022

text: Alexander Graham Bell first sent clear speech by telephone in 1876, calling to his assistant: “Mr. Watson—come here—I want to see you.”
In 1877 Thomas Edison tested a machine for recording the human voice by speaking into it the line ‘Mary had a little lamb’.

source.label: National Park Service, Thomas Edison National Historical Park

text: Italy has the European Union’s oldest first-time mothers: in 2024, women there had their first child at 31.9 years on average.
Physicist Sally Ride became the first American woman in space on 18 June 1983, flying aboard the space shuttle Challenger.
Vocabulary keeps growing through adulthood: between 20 and 60, an average native speaker of American English learns about one new word every two days.

source.label: Brysbaert et al., Frontiers in Psychology, 2016

text: Martin Luther King Jr. gave his “I Have a Dream” speech in 1963, speaking to more than 200,000 people gathered in Washington.

source.label: Martin Luther King Jr. Research and Education Institute, Stanford

text: The US Constitution makes 35 the youngest age at which a person may become President.

source.label: US Constitution, Article II, Section 1 (National Archives transcript)

text: Metabolism holds steady through adulthood: adjusted for body size, the energy a person burns each day stays stable from 20 to 60, even during pregnancy.
In 1944 mathematician Grace Hopper, who had left teaching to join the US Navy, was assigned to Harvard, where her team worked on the Mark I, an early computer.

source.label: National Women's History Museum, Grace Hopper

text: People stay attached to the music of their youth: a study of 4,824 people from 102 countries found this ‘musical reminiscence bump’ in every age group.
The Fields Medal, which recognises outstanding mathematical achievement, is kept for the young: a candidate’s 40th birthday must not fall before 1 January of the award year.
In the Analects, Confucius looks back on his life in stages. Of forty he says simply: ‘At forty, I had no doubts.’

source.label: Chinese Text Project, Analects, Wei Zheng 2.4 (James Legge translation)

text: Rudyard Kipling received the 1907 Nobel Prize in Literature, and remains the youngest person ever awarded it.
On 1 December 1955, Rosa Parks, a 42-year-old seamstress, was arrested in Montgomery, Alabama, for refusing to give up her seat on a city bus.

source.label: US National Archives, The Arrest Records of Rosa Parks

text: In 1960, at 43, John F. Kennedy won the US presidency, becoming the youngest person ever elected to that office.

source.label: Miller Center, University of Virginia, John F. Kennedy: Life in Brief

text: Half of all people in the European Union are older than 44.9 and half are younger, the EU’s median age on 1 January 2025.
Many people first notice around age 45 that they hold a page a little farther away to read it, as the lens of the eye slowly loses its flexibility.

source.label: MedlinePlus (US National Library of Medicine), Presbyopia, 2026

text: In 1982 the typical American jazz concertgoer was 29. By 2008 the median age of the jazz audience had risen to 46.

source.label: National Endowment for the Arts, Arts Participation 2008 (SPPA)

text: Reading other people’s emotions is a late-blooming skill: in a study of nearly 50,000 people it peaked in the 40s or 50s, long after processing speed and short-term memory.

source.label: Association for Psychological Science, on Hartshorne & Germine (Psychological Science), 2015

text: Across 145 countries, well-being follows a U-shaped curve through adulthood, dipping to its lowest point in midlife, on average around age 48, then rising again.
A 2015 study put the median age at which American women become grandmothers at 49. In parts of Western Europe it came up to eight years later.
In October 1966 the Carnatic singer M. S. Subbulakshmi gave a recital of Indian songs in the United Nations General Assembly Hall in New York.

source.label: UN Photo, Celebration of United Nations Day 1966

text: In surveys of over 1.5 million Americans, everyday stress stayed high from the 20s until about age 50, then fell steeply through the 70s.

source.label: Stone, Schneider & Broderick, Journal of Psychosomatic Research, 2017

text: Rabindranath Tagore, a writer of poems, songs, stories and plays in Bengali, won the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature for verse recast in his own English words.
Women’s voices often deepen in midlife: one study found the voices of women aged 40 to 60 were pitched 34 to 38 Hz lower than those of women aged 20 to 30.

source.label: Eichhorn, Kent, Austin et al., Journal of Voice, 2018

text: In a worldwide survey of 4,192 people, published in 2012, 74% of those aged 45 to 65 had some grey hair; when it arrives varies with ethnic and geographic origin.

source.label: Panhard, Lozano & Loussouarn, British Journal of Dermatology, 2012

text: Among adults aged 45 to 65, musicians were better than non-musicians at following speech against background noise, a 2011 study found.

source.label: Parbery-Clark, Strait, Anderson, Hittner & Kraus, PLOS ONE, 2011

text: In the US in 2025, the median age of farmers, ranchers and agricultural managers was 56.1, compared with 42.1 for all employed people.

source.label: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey table 11b, 2025

text: In January 1955 the contralto Marian Anderson became the first African American soloist to sing at New York’s Metropolitan Opera.
Across OECD countries, the share of people aged 55 to 64 in work rose from 46.1% in 2002 to 64.6% in 2022.
In January 2026, US workers aged 55 to 64 had been with their current employer for a median of 9.6 years, more than three times as long as those aged 25 to 34.

source.label: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employee Tenure, January 2026

text: In the Analects, Confucius says that at sixty his ear became “an obedient organ for the reception of truth”.

source.label: Chinese Text Project, Analects, Wei Zheng 2.4 (James Legge translation)

text: In 1991, American retirees said they had stopped working at 57 on average. By 2022 the average retirement age they reported had risen to 61.
A man’s speaking voice is usually at its lowest between 40 and 50; by 60 to 70 it has risen back to the pitch of his twenties.

source.label: Skoog Waller & Eriksson, Frontiers in Psychology, 2016

text: Across OECD countries in 2022, the average normal retirement age was 63.6 for women and 64.4 for men.
In a 10-year study of daily emotions, the balance of positive over negative feelings kept improving with age, peaking at around 64.

source.label: Carstensen et al., Psychology and Aging, 2011

text: In 2018, for the first time in history, people aged 65 or over outnumbered children under five worldwide.
In the 2020 US census, about 1 in 6 people were 65 or older. A century earlier, in 1920, fewer than 1 in 20 were.
In an 18-month German trial, dancers averaging 67 years old gained volume in the brain’s memory hub and, unlike a fitness group, clearly improved their balance.

source.label: Rehfeld et al., Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 2017

text: Vocabulary is a late bloomer: in a large online study of mental skills, it peaked when participants were in their late 60s or early 70s.
In a German-Swiss trial of adults aged 62 to 78, six months of piano lessons improved hearing of speech in noise in the left ear, a gain not seen in a music-listening group.

source.label: Worschech et al., Frontiers in Neuroscience, 2021

text: In 2025 Denmark voted to raise its state pension age to 70, the highest in Europe, for people born after 1970.
In a US trial with 390 adults averaging 71 years old, six months of singing in a community choir eased loneliness and raised interest in life.

source.label: Johnson et al., Journals of Gerontology: Series B, 2020 (PubMed)

text: In a UK survey of over 300,000 adults in 2012 to 2015, people aged 65 to 74 reported the highest average happiness of any age group.
Cuban singer Ibrahim Ferrer won Best New Artist at the very first Latin Grammy Awards, held in September 2000.

source.label: Billboard, 25 Years of Latin Grammys timeline, 2024

text: Adults in their 70s who had exercised for five decades had muscle capillaries and aerobic enzymes matching those of 25-year-old exercisers.

source.label: Gries et al., Journal of Applied Physiology, 2018 (PubMed)

text: Nelson Mandela voted for the first time in his life on 27 April 1994, and on 10 May became South Africa’s first democratically elected president.
In the US in 2024, people aged 75 and over spent an average of 46 minutes a day reading for pleasure. Those aged 15 to 19 read for 9 minutes.

source.label: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey 2024 (via FRASER)

text: John Glenn returned to space aboard Discovery in 1998, 36 years after his first orbit, and took part in research on space flight and ageing.

source.label: NASA, Biography of John H. Glenn

text: Brenda Lee’s ‘Rockin’ Around the Christmas Tree’, recorded when she was 13, reached No. 1 on the US Hot 100 in December 2023.
In the US in 2024, adults aged 75 and over spent 7.6 hours a day on leisure and sports, more than any other age group.

source.label: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey 2024 (via FRASER)

text: Yuichiro Miura reached the summit of Everest on 23 May 2013, becoming the oldest man to climb it, a record he had first set in 2003.

source.label: Guinness World Records, Oldest person to climb Everest (male)

text: In the decades-long Seattle Longitudinal Study, fewer than half of 81-year-olds showed reliable mental decline over the preceding seven years.

source.label: Schaie & Willis, The Seattle Longitudinal Study of Adult Cognitive Development, ISSBD Bulletin, 2010

text: Some people over 80, dubbed SuperAgers, have unusually strong memories and a patch of brain cortex thicker than that of healthy 50- to 60-year-olds.

source.label: Rogalski et al., Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience, 2013 (PubMed)

text: Sumiko Iwamuro, who went to DJ school at 77, was recognised in 2018 as the world’s oldest female club DJ, playing monthly in Tokyo.

source.label: Guinness World Records, Oldest club DJ (female)

text: Some local government offices and financial institutions in Japan use earphones that vibrate the ear’s cartilage, so staff helping older people need not speak loudly.

source.label: Cabinet Office of Japan, Annual Report on the Ageing Society FY2025

text: In 2018, the UK’s Office for National Statistics projected that the number of people aged 85 and over would double, from 1.6 million in 2016 to 3.2 million by 2041.

source.label: Office for National Statistics (UK), Living longer, 2018

text: In the UK in 2016 to 2017, 8% of people aged 85 and over were providing informal care to others.

source.label: Office for National Statistics (UK), Living longer, 2018

text: Scottish volunteers born in 1921 retook, at 87, a mental ability test they had first sat at 11, and their childhood scores still predicted their results.

source.label: Gow et al., Psychology and Aging, 2011 (PubMed)

text: In a study of adults aged 20 to 93, people who sang often kept the steadiness of their pitch and loudness with age, unlike non-singers.

source.label: Lortie et al., Journal of Voice, 2017 (PubMed)

text: Folk singer Pete Seeger performed at the concert celebrating Barack Obama’s inauguration in January 2009, months before his 90th birthday.
In Japan, turning 90 is called sotsuju, because the shorthand form of the character 卒, written 卆, looks like 九十, the numerals for ninety.

source.label: Nippon.com, Japanese Names for Age Milestones, 2024

text: In January 2024 composer John Williams, 91, broke his own record as the oldest person nominated for a competitive Oscar, for his Indiana Jones score.
In a 1998 survey of 2,262 Danes aged 92 or 93, 74% said they were always or almost always satisfied with their lives.

source.label: Nybo et al., Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, 2001 (PubMed)

text: Singer Charles Aznavour received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in August 2017, aged 93, and was still writing songs and performing.

source.label: Hollywood Walk of Fame (Hollywood Chamber of Commerce), 2017

text: South Korea’s Song Hae, host of the TV show National Singing Contest since 1988, was certified in April 2022, aged 94, as the oldest TV music talent show host.
Nola Ochs of Kansas graduated from college in May 2007, aged 95, alongside her 21-year-old granddaughter, becoming the world’s oldest college graduate.
In a 1990 study, nine frail nursing-home residents aged up to 96 did eight weeks of weight training, and their strength rose by 174% on average.
Bluesman Pinetop Perkins won a Grammy in February 2011, aged 97, becoming the oldest Grammy winner.
In a study of 29 people aged 90 to 101 in rural southern Italy, the elders reported better mental well-being than their younger relatives.
Captain Tom Moore reached number one in the UK singles chart on 24 April 2020, aged 99, with ‘You’ll Never Walk Alone’, recorded with Michael Ball.
Japan counted 153 people aged 100 or over in 1963. In 2026 it counted 107,677.
Cuban-born painter Carmen Herrera had a solo exhibition at New York’s Whitney Museum in 2016, aged 101, and was still working in her studio almost every day.
Ingeborg Rapoport, barred by the Nazis from defending her doctorate in 1938, finally passed the exam in Hamburg in May 2015, aged 102.
Sweden’s Rut Larsson made a tandem parachute jump in May 2022, aged 103 years and 259 days, setting the Guinness record for the oldest woman to make one.
The United Nations estimated that about 722,000 people worldwide were aged 100 or older in 2024.
Eileen Ash, who first played Test cricket for England in 1937, rang the bell at Lord’s before the 2017 Women’s World Cup final, aged 105.
British nationals can receive a birthday message from the King at 100 and 105, and then every year after their 105th birthday.
French pianist Colette Maze, who began playing at 5, was still recording her albums at home at 107, usually on Sundays, when the building was quieter.
In Japan, 108 is chaju, ‘tea longevity’, because the character for tea, 茶, can be split into 十, 十 and 八十八: 10 + 10 + 88.
Hikaru Kato of Kumamoto, Japan, kept writing letters to local newspapers about his war experiences, each time hoping war would never return, until he was 109.
Gerontologists call anyone validated as having reached 110 a supercentenarian.
After becoming the world’s oldest man in 2024, aged 111, Liverpool-born retired accountant John Tinniswood still listened to the radio for the news and managed his own finances.
A supercentenarian tested at ages 112 and 113 performed above the average for healthy adults aged 60 to 75 on psychological tests.

source.label: den Dunnen et al., Neurobiology of Aging, 2008 (PubMed)

text: Yisrael Kristal, who missed his bar mitzvah at 13 because of the First World War, finally celebrated it in 2016, aged 113, among his great-grandchildren.
Chiyo Miyako, who trained as a telegraph operator, was still practising calligraphy and writing haiku at 114.
Sequencing the blood of a 115-year-old woman suggested that most of her white blood cells descended from just two related blood stem cells.
Jiroemon Kimura of Kyotango, Japan, celebrated his 116th birthday in April 2013, the first man verified to reach that age.
When Nabi Tajima of Japan’s Kikai Island turned 117 in 2017, her family spanned five generations below her, down to 14 great-great-great-grandchildren.
Sister André, a French nun who spent 28 years caring for orphans and elderly people in Vichy, became the world’s oldest living person in April 2022, aged 118.
Japan’s Kane Tanaka, who enjoyed board games, maths problems and chocolate, reached 119 on 2 January 2022.
The Book of Genesis sets the days allowed to humankind at ‘one hundred and twenty years’.
For her 121st birthday in February 1996, Jeanne Calment released a CD, ‘Time’s Mistress’, reminiscing over rap and other music.
Jeanne Calment of Arles, France, born in 1875, lived to 122 years and 164 days, the greatest fully verified age of any human.
